Good evening, everyone. My name is Jorge Matos, and I am a cancer survivor. Ten years ago, I was a patient on the fourth floor of this hospital. I have been cancer-free since 2016, and I have been a volunteer here for six years. Every Tuesday, I sit with patients who are starting their treatment. I tell them my story, and I listen to theirs. My mentor here was Marta, the patient navigator. I have known her for ten years, and she has never stopped helping people. Tonight, the network celebrates its fifteenth anniversary, and I want to say one thing: thank you for my second life.

Hi Fernando, it's Sarah. I just read the anniversary newsletter. Congratulations! Fifteen years is a long time. And I didn't know this: you have worked at Einstein for twenty-four years! That's amazing. Our program in Texas is younger. We have had the family apartments since 2019, so only for seven years. I have a question for you, too. How long has Marta worked with patients? I want to invite her to speak at our conference in May. She is exactly the kind of mentor that our new nurses need. Call me when you can. Bye!
